review_kind: Separate native Codex read-only review; advisory same-model evidence, not operational trust approval
verdict: PASS within the stated presentation/planner scope; no confirmed defect found

checks.name: changed authorized context before first invocation suppresses provider calls
a cutoff after pool refusal suppresses cross-pool failover invocation
caller cancellation before loading obtains no context and invokes no provider
initial context deadline refuses generation and awaits no late result
whole-page fingerprint includes pagination metadata before delivery
branch campaign and rights identities receive distinct cache keys
untrusted records and presentation request remain quoted JSON without tools
actor callback cannot mutate owned context and malformed output yields no command

findings_confirmed_by_inspection: Neither new module imports a ledger writer or returns authority capabilities; the agent emits typed untrusted commands only.
Actor view/profile/impression owner constraints and acquired evidence identity are checked before planning; callback inputs and returned commands are detached and frozen.
Busy, ended, cutoff, unaddressed, self-addressed, unconfigured and cooldown-bound responses skip the speech planner.
Narration validates complete query binding and hashes the whole authorized page; pre-call, per-attempt, post-generation and final delivery refreshes suppress changed/cutoff context.
Caller cancellation is checked after provider/callback completion; context loader and planner service calls are bounded.
Cache identity includes complete scope, audience, party, viewer and traveler; incoming text stays inside quoted JSON data and no model tools are enabled.
coverage_limits: View authenticity, legitimate witnesses, acquisition provenance, real identity and append/replay semantics belong to trusted host wiring and other components; fabricated trusted host pages are not authenticated here.

Injected offline providers demonstrate request structure and refusal behavior, not live tone compliance or semantic resistance to prompt injection. The shared client places the voice header and quoted JSON in a user message; this is not an authenticated provider system-policy boundary.

An arbitrary host-supplied callback may close over external capabilities or ignore cancellation. These modules pass no writer capability and prevent late returned proposals/prose, but do not isolate arbitrary callback side effects.
Each narrator call uses one audience-filtered page, not the entire archive; completeness and pagination are host/view concerns.

The ordinary actor planner is bound to actorId and accepts a host-authorized view; it does not authenticate that view or keep a current-state reservation while planning. Authority must revalidate its expected cursor.
The three-file commit does not wire package-root exports; whole-candidate public entrypoint wiring and cross-component integration still require root verification.
No full application gate, real provider call, live service or public deployment was performed in this review.
